title: SYNDACTYLY, TYPE III
alt_titles: SYNDACTYLY OF FINGERS IV AND V

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that syndactyly type III (SDTY3) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gap junction protein alpha-1 gene (GJA1; 121014), which encodes connexin-43, on chromosome 6q22. Type III syndactyly is also a characteristic feature of oculodentodigital dysplasia, which is caused by mutation in the same gene.

checks.claim: Syndactyly type III (SDTY3) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GJA1 gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract reports GJA1 mutations only in oculodentodigital dysplasia families. It does not address isolated syndactyly type III or zygosity.

checks.claim: The GJA1 gene encodes connexin-43.
checks.evidence_quote: The human connexin 43 gene, or GJA1, is located at human chromosome 6q22-q23
checks.explanation: The abstract states that GJA1 is the connexin 43 gene.

checks.claim: The GJA1 gene is located on chromosome 6q22.
checks.evidence_quote: The human connexin 43 gene, or GJA1, is located at human chromosome 6q22-q23
checks.explanation: The location is consistent with the paper; restating a gene's chromosomal location counts as standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: Type III syndactyly is a characteristic feature of oculodentodigital dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: A family is described with type III syndactyly and facies resembling the oculodentodigital dysplasia facial phenotype in the absence of any of the other characteristic findings of the latter condition.
checks.explanation: The phrase 'other characteristic findings' implies that type III syndactyly is a characteristic finding of oculodentodigital dysplasia.

checks.claim: Oculodentodigital dysplasia is caused by mutation in the GJA1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We found mutations in the GJA1 gene in all 17 families with oculodentodigital dysplasia that we screened.
checks.explanation: The paper directly states this.

paragraphs.text: Syndactyly type III is a limb malformation in which the ring and little fingers (fingers 4 and 5) are joined, usually completely and on both hands. The fusion is usually of soft tissue only, but the distal phalanges are sometimes fused as well. The little finger is often short, with a small or missing middle phalanx. The feet are usually not affected. In the Temtamy and McKusick classification of syndactylies, this pattern is listed as type III.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the ring and little fingers (fingers 4 and 5) are joined.
checks.evidence_quote: Five new cases of isolated syndactyly of the small and ring finger are described.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes syndactyly of the ring and small (little) fingers.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the fusion of the ring and little fingers is usually complete.
checks.evidence_quote: complete cutaneous syndactyly of fingers 3-5 in the left hand and fingers 4-5 in the right hand
checks.explanation: The syndactyly was complete in this one patient. The abstract does not say fusion is usually complete in general.

checks.claim: Syndactyly type III usually affects both hands.
checks.evidence_quote: complete cutaneous syndactyly of fingers 3-5 in the left hand and fingers 4-5 in the right hand
checks.explanation: Both hands were affected in this one patient. The abstract does not say both hands are usually affected in general.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the fusion is usually of soft tissue only.
checks.explanation: The fusion was cutaneous (soft tissue) in this case. The abstract makes no general statement that fusion is usually soft tissue only.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the distal phalanges of the ring and little fingers are sometimes fused.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not mention fusion of the distal phalanges.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the little finger is often short, with a small or missing middle phalanx.
checks.evidence_quote: Brachymesophalangia of the fifth finger is a frequent association.
checks.explanation: Brachymesophalangia (a short middle phalanx) of the fifth finger is reported as frequent. A missing middle phalanx is not mentioned.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the feet are usually not affected.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not say whether the feet are affected.

checks.claim: In the Temtamy and McKusick classification of syndactylies, fusion of the ring and little fingers is listed as type III.
checks.evidence_quote: familial syndactyly of the ring and little finger (Type III syndactyly)
checks.explanation: The abstract calls ring–little finger syndactyly 'Type III' but does not name the Temtamy and McKusick classification.

paragraphs.text: The ring and little fingers are joined, usually on both hands. The little finger is typically short because its middle phalanx is small or absent. The toes are usually normal. The same hand defect occurs in oculodentodigital dysplasia, where it comes with eye, tooth and other limb anomalies. This has raised the question of whether isolated type III syndactyly is a separate condition or the mildest end of the oculodentodigital dysplasia spectrum.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the ring and little fingers are joined, usually on both hands.
checks.evidence_quote: Syndactyly of the ring and little finger.
checks.explanation: The title supports that the ring and little fingers are joined. It does not say this is usually on both hands.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the little finger is typically short because its middle phalanx is small or absent.
checks.evidence_quote: Brachymesophalangia of the fifth finger is a frequent association.
checks.explanation: A short middle phalanx of the fifth finger is reported as frequent. An absent middle phalanx is not mentioned.

checks.claim: In syndactyly type III, the toes are usually normal.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not describe the toes.

checks.claim: The type III syndactyly hand defect occurs in oculodentodigital dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Syndactyly type III and conductive deafness can occur in some cases
checks.explanation: The abstract says type III syndactyly occurs in oculodentodigital dysplasia.

checks.claim: In oculodentodigital dysplasia, type III syndactyly occurs together with eye, tooth and other limb anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: This autosomal dominant syndrome presents with craniofacial (ocular, nasal, and dental) and limb dysmorphisms, spastic paraplegia, and neurodegeneration. Syndactyly type III and conductive deafness can occur in some cases
checks.explanation: Oculodentodigital dysplasia includes eye, tooth and limb anomalies, and syndactyly type III occurs within it.

checks.claim: Whether isolated type III syndactyly is a separate condition or the mildest end of the oculodentodigital dysplasia spectrum has been questioned.
checks.evidence_quote: Oculodentodigital dysplasia and type III syndactyly: separate genetic entities or disease spectrum?
checks.explanation: The title poses exactly this question, and the abstract says the relationship between the two conditions is discussed.

paragraphs.text: Syndactyly type III is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.

checks.claim: Syndactyly type III is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that inheritance is autosomal dominant.

paragraphs.text: Heterozygous mutations in the GJA1 gene, which encodes connexin-43, have been found in families with type III syndactyly. Some of these families also had features of oculodentodigital dysplasia, which is caused by GJA1 mutation. Richardson et al. (2004) showed that, in the developing mouse, Gja1 is expressed in tissues that match the features of oculodentodigital syndrome and type III syndactyly.

checks.claim: Heterozygous mutations in the GJA1 gene have been found in families with type III syndactyly.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied; it does not mention mutations found in families.

checks.claim: The GJA1 gene encodes connexin-43.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied; it does not mention connexin-43.

checks.claim: Some families with type III syndactyly and GJA1 mutations also had features of oculodentodigital dysplasia.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied; it does not describe any families.

checks.claim: Oculodentodigital dysplasia is caused by GJA1 mutation.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied; it does not say that GJA1 mutation causes ODD.

checks.claim: Richardson et al. (2004) showed that in the developing mouse, Gja1 is expressed in tissues that match the features of oculodentodigital syndrome and type III syndactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: Expression of Gja1 correlates with the phenotype observed in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.
checks.explanation: The title supports the claim that Gja1 expression correlates with the ODD/SDTY3 phenotype. It does not specify the developing mouse, which may be in the unsupplied full text.
